title: "Data exploration"

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```



```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(quanteda)
library(quanteda.textstats)
library(udpipe)
```

```{r}
# 1. Identify all text files in the working directory
files <- list.files(pattern = "\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)

# Verify corpus size 
cat("Total files found:", length(files), "\n")

# 2. Ingest texts into a structured tibble and normalize Early Modern typography
corpus_df <- tibble(file_path = files) %>%
  mutate(
    # Extract document identifier from filename (without extension)
    doc_id = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file_path)),
    # Read text content
    text_raw = map_chr(file_path, ~ read_file(.x)),
    
    # REQUIRED STEP: Normalize the Early Modern long S character ('ſ' -> 's')
    text_clean = str_replace_all(text_raw, "ſ", "s")
  )

# 3. Verification: Ensure all long S characters are eliminated
cat("Remaining long S count:", sum(str_count(corpus_df$text_clean, "ſ")), "(expected: 0)\n")
```

```{r approach1-tfidf, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Approach 1: TF-IDF Lexical Distinctiveness
# ==============================================================================

# 1. Build a quanteda corpus from cleaned texts
corp <- corpus(corpus_df, docid_field = "doc_id", text_field = "text_clean")

# 2. Tokenize: lowercase, remove punctuation, numbers, symbols, and standard English stopwords
toks <- tokens(corp, 
               remove_punct = TRUE, 
               remove_numbers = TRUE, 
               remove_symbols = TRUE) %>%
  tokens_tolower() %>%
  tokens_remove(stopwords("en"))

# 3. Construct Document-Feature Matrix (DFM) and compute TF-IDF weights
dfm_counts <- dfm(toks)
dfm_tfidf_mat <- dfm_tfidf(dfm_counts)

# 4. Extract top 10 distinctive terms for each document
top_terms_list <- list()

for (doc in docnames(dfm_tfidf_mat)) {
  # Sort features by TF-IDF weight descending
  sorted_weights <- sort(as.matrix(dfm_tfidf_mat[doc, ])[1, ], decreasing = TRUE)
  top10 <- head(sorted_weights, 10)
  
  top_terms_list[[doc]] <- tibble(
    doc_id = doc,
    rank = 1:10,
    term = names(top10),
    tfidf = round(as.numeric(top10), 3)
  )
}

# Combine into a single tidy dataframe
top_tfidf_df <- bind_rows(top_terms_list)

# Reshape into a wide comparison table (Documents as rows, Top terms 1-10 as columns)
top_terms_wide <- top_tfidf_df %>%
  select(doc_id, rank, term) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = rank, names_prefix = "top_", values_from = term)

# Display the top distinctive terms table
print(top_terms_wide, n = 23)
```

```{r approach2-pearson-heatmap, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Approach 2: Pearson Correlation and Similarity Heatmap
# ==============================================================================

# 1. Trim very rare terms (min_termfreq = 5) to mitigate typographical/OCR noise
dfm_trimmed <- dfm_trim(dfm_counts, min_termfreq = 5)

# 2. Pairwise Pearson correlations between all documents
sim_r <- textstat_simil(dfm_trimmed, margin = "documents", method = "correlation")

# Convert similarity object to matrix and round for visual clarity
r_mat <- round(as.matrix(sim_r), 3)

# 3. Reshape correlation matrix to long format for ggplot
heat_df <- as.data.frame(r_mat) %>%
  rownames_to_column("doc_i") %>%
  pivot_longer(-doc_i, names_to = "doc_j", values_to = "r")

# 4. Create the similarity heatmap
ggplot(heat_df, aes(x = doc_j, y = doc_i, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile() +
  coord_fixed() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "red",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Pearson Correlation Between Documents",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Correlation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

# 5. Extract the Two Most Similar and Two Least Similar Document Pairs
# Filter out self-correlations (doc_i == doc_j) and avoid duplicate symmetrical pairs
pairs_df <- heat_df %>%
  filter(doc_i < doc_j) %>%
  arrange(desc(r))

cat("--- Top 2 Most Similar Document Pairs ---\n")
print(head(pairs_df, 2))

cat("\n--- Top 2 Least Similar Document Pairs ---\n")
print(tail(pairs_df, 2))
```

```{r approach3-setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Approach 3 - Step 1: Model Setup & Document Filtering
# ==============================================================================

library(udpipe)

# 1. Download and load English UDPipe language model
udmodel <- udpipe_download_model(language = "english-ewt")
udmodel <- udpipe_load_model(udmodel$file_model)

# 2. Filter corpus for the least similar document pair (r = 0.170)
selected_docs <- corpus_df %>%
  filter(doc_id %in% c("A93819", "B14801__Free_Trade"))

# Check selected documents
selected_docs %>% select(doc_id)
```
```{r approach3-parsing, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Approach 3 - Step 2: Dependency Parsing
# ==============================================================================

# Annotate texts using dependency parsing
annotated_texts <- udpipe_annotate(
  udmodel, 
  x = selected_docs$text_clean, 
  doc_id = selected_docs$doc_id
) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Quick inspection of parsed tokens
head(annotated_texts %>% select(doc_id, sentence_id, token, upos, dep_rel), 10)
```

```{r approach3-metrics, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Approach 3 - Step 3: Compute Week 05 Complexity Metrics
# ==============================================================================

syntactic_summary <- annotated_texts %>%
  group_by(doc_id) %>%
  summarize(
    num_sentences = n_distinct(sentence_id),
    num_words = sum(!upos %in% c("PUNCT", "SYM")),
    
    # Clause heads
    num_clauses = sum(dep_rel %in% c("root", "conj", "advcl", "acl", "ccomp", "xcomp") & 
                        upos %in% c("VERB", "AUX")),
    
    # Dependent clauses
    num_dep_clauses = sum(dep_rel %in% c("advcl", "acl", "ccomp", "xcomp")),
    
    # Coordination
    num_coordination = sum(dep_rel %in% c("conj", "cc")),
    
    # Complex nominals
    num_complex_nominals = sum(dep_rel %in% c("compound", "nmod", "amod") & 
                                 upos %in% c("NOUN", "ADJ")),
    
    # --- Normalized Metrics ---
    MLS = round(num_words / num_sentences, 2),
    C_S = round(num_clauses / num_sentences, 2),
    DC_S = round(num_dep_clauses / num_sentences, 2),
    Coord_S = round(num_coordination / num_sentences, 2),
    CN_S = round(num_complex_nominals / num_sentences, 2)
  )

# Display required summary table
print(syntactic_summary %>% select(doc_id, MLS, C_S, DC_S, Coord_S, CN_S))
```
```{r approach3-examples, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Approach 3 - Step 4: Extract Illustrative Sentences
# ==============================================================================

example_sentences <- annotated_texts %>%
  filter(!upos %in% c("PUNCT", "SYM")) %>%
  group_by(doc_id, sentence_id, sentence) %>%
  summarize(sentence_length = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(doc_id) %>%
  slice_max(sentence_length, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

for(i in 1:nrow(example_sentences)) {
  cat("\n=======================================================\n")
  cat("Document:", example_sentences$doc_id[i], "\n")
  cat("Word Count:", example_sentences$sentence_length[i], "\n")
  cat("Sentence Text:\n", example_sentences$sentence[i], "\n")
}
```
